description_short.value: Ghanaian cocoa-buying company, about 75% owned by SSNIT and the Government of Ghana, whose purchases have collapsed since 2023; suspended from the Ghana Stock Exchange since November 2023, with liabilities far above its assets.
description_short.source: Written by us from the PBC Limited financial statements for the year ended 30 September 2025 (GSE PR 393/2026: report of the directors, consolidated statements of comprehensive income and financial position) and GSE PR 401/2023 (suspension of listing status)

description_full.value: PBC Limited, formerly the Produce Buying Company, buys cocoa beans from farmers, stores them in sheds at village and society level, and carts them to collection points where the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) inspects, grades and seals them. It was the cocoa-buying arm of COCOBOD before being incorporated as a separate company on 15 September 1999 and listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange in May 2000. It also owns Golden Bean Hotel Limited, a hotel business. The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT, 38.1%) and the Ministry of Finance (36.7%) together own about 75% of its 480 million shares, and the government also holds a golden preference share. Revenue, which is mostly the value of cocoa bought and delivered, fell from GHS 1.26 billion in the year to September 2021 and GHS 779 million in 2023 to GHS 41 million in 2024, and was GHS 64 million in 2025. The group has made a loss every year since 2021 (GHS 39.8 million in 2025), and its liabilities, mainly long-term loans of about GHS 318 million, exceed its assets: equity was negative GHS 481 million at September 2025. The auditors qualified their opinion on the 2025 accounts over going concern and noted that title deeds to the sheds and buildings ceded to the company by COCOBOD in 1999 have not been seen. The Ghana Stock Exchange suspended the shares from 8 November 2023 because no results had been filed since September 2022; the company has since filed its accounts for 2023 to 2025, but the shares remained suspended. A new board, chaired by Nana Meisu Adu, with Seidu Yonye as managing director, was appointed on 31 July 2025.
